abstract: Continuous autoregressive speech language models combine an autoregressive (AR) backbone with a diffusion or flow-matching head. Preference post-training requires choosing how to construct pairs and which modules to update. Controlled interventions show that a perturbed acoustic patch changes subsequent backbone states, yet larger representation changes do not necessarily reduce speech quality. We construct preference pairs through noise or inference-configuration perturbations and formulate a preference update based on reference-relative flow-matching errors. Updating the backbone with a fixed head yields stronger reward improvements than head-only adaptation in our evaluated setting. Across flow-time and module ablations, the lowest training loss does not consistently produce the best speech. These findings support preference post-training that considers both acoustic sampling and autoregressive conditioning, with training choices validated on generated utterances.

oneSentenceThesis: 论文研究连续自回归语音模型在偏好后训练中如何构造偏好对、在哪个流噪声水平比较以及更新自回归主干还是声学头，发现固定声学头只更新主干后部层在所测条件下带来更大的自动奖励提升，但训练损失更低并不等于生成语音更好。
